correctness.rationale: For every support with at most n−2 cells, inclusion-exclusion over negative cells reduces the signed trace count to sums of signs over completions of at most n−2 fixed assignments, each annihilated by a sign-reversing transposition of two unassigned images. A one-factorization leaves at least two valid completions for every matching positive trace and hence one of each parity. At n−1 cells only the full inclusion-exclusion term can survive: for a near-perfect matching it is the unique completion sign times (−1) raised to the number of negative answers. Each adaptive leaf of depth n−1 has signed mass at most one, with at most 2^(n−1) leaves; a fixed near-perfect matching attains this exact bound and gives TV 2^(n−1)/n!. Nonmatching supports cannot be shattered, and for n−1 disjoint cells one parity fails the all-positive trace while the other fails a single-negative trace. A positive query branch reduces to a parity coset on n−1 rows, giving Ldim=n−2 by induction. Both finite enumerators replayed successfully through n=6, and a separate minimax tree verifier passed n=2,3,4; these calculations are corroboration, not infinite proof.

value.rationale: Parity restriction is a canonical statistical and combinatorial constraint on permutation assignments. The first-observable-depth problem asks precisely when a sequence of membership observations can distinguish the two equally numerous sign cosets, and how much information survives optimally with adaptive testing. The exact signed boundary law gives the complete optimal TV and Bayes risk, not merely textbook (n−2)-transitivity; the same theorem identifies the full VC shattering complex and online dimension and contrasts a different, previously studied matching-deletion restriction. Both the all-order information threshold and its tight adaptive constant have mathematical motivation independent of the finite verifiers.
